question: Should OpenClaw core commit to local, container, reverse-proxy, and node-mode as named release-tested hosting profiles with these readiness requirements?
rationale: The implementation is coherent, but profile naming, required conditions, configuration surfaces, and fail-closed semantics create a permanent core support matrix that code review cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve after foundation
options.body: Approve or adjust the matrix in the RFC, land the readiness dependency, and rebase this PR for a profile-only review.

options.title: Keep readiness generic
options.body: Use operator-selected readiness criteria without adding named core profiles or a hosting.profile configuration surface.

options.title: Defer the matrix
options.body: Pause or close this PR until maintainer-owned deployment demand justifies standardized core profiles.

recommendation.title: Approve after foundation
recommendation.body: Approve or adjust the matrix in the RFC, land the readiness dependency, and rebase this PR for a profile-only review.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal connects this person to the current Gateway readiness implementation that the proposal extends.
